title: The Wedding Was a Lie—And the Pregnant Woman Was Hiding a Secret That Changed Everything

blocks.text: Twelve days before my wedding, I discovered that the man I loved had been living a second life.
But the truth was far worse than an affair.
My name is Eden Rowe. I was twenty-nine years old, and until that morning, I had been completely convinced that Carter Vale was the man I would spend the rest of my life with.
Carter was charming, successful, and attentive. He remembered tiny details about me, brought me coffee when I worked late, and always kissed my forehead before leaving for work.
His mother, Margaret, had initially seemed equally wonderful.
She welcomed me into the family, helped me choose my wedding dress, and insisted on paying for the reception at the family’s prestigious country club.
I didn’t know I was walking into a carefully constructed lie.
That morning, Margaret and I were choosing our final wedding invitations at an expensive stationery boutique downtown.
Carter was supposedly attending a series of business meetings in another state, approximately 800 miles away.
“Just twelve more days, sweetheart,” he’d said. “Then nothing will ever keep us apart.”
I smiled at the memory while examining the gold lettering on our invitations.
Then I looked through the enormous storefront window.
He was carrying two shopping bags from a baby clothing store.
His other arm was wrapped around Brielle Sloane, his childhood friend.
I recognized her immediately. Carter had spoken about her countless times, always describing her as a sister.
He had even told me she was going through a difficult period and needed support.
But the way he held her wasn’t brotherly.
He leaned forward and kissed her forehead.
Then Brielle placed his hand against her stomach.
“You have no idea what’s at stake, Eden. Whatever you think you saw, forget it.”
“Your son is supposed to be in another state.”
Hundreds of beautiful cards, each carrying our names.
I picked them up, walked to the garbage bin, and dropped every single one inside.
“Canceling a wedding I apparently know nothing about.”
I grabbed my purse and headed toward the door.
But before I could reach it, someone called my name.
She had crossed the street and hurried into the boutique.
Her face was pale, and tears were running down her cheeks.
She reached into her purse and pulled out a sealed envelope.
“Please read this before you make any decisions.”
“Then why was he holding you like that?”
“Because he’s been protecting me. And because your wedding has something to do with what happened to my family.”
My mother had died when I was seventeen.
And Brielle had just told me something I couldn’t understand.
I opened the envelope with trembling fingers.
Inside was a photograph of two women standing outside a hospital.
The other was a woman I recognized from Brielle’s childhood photographs.
For the day Eden finally discovers the truth.
“Eden, if you are reading this, it means Margaret has finally arranged the marriage she promised would happen. Please don’t sign anything until you know who your father really was.”
I had been told my father abandoned my mother before I was born.
She had raised me alone, and whenever I asked about him, she changed the subject.
“Your mother and mine were best friends. They worked together at a financial firm owned by Carter’s grandfather.”
“What does that have to do with my wedding?”
“Twenty years ago, Carter’s grandfather transferred ownership of a valuable property portfolio into a private trust. Your mother discovered that someone had been stealing money from it.”
The boutique suddenly felt unbearably quiet.
“No,” Brielle replied. “And you know it.”
My future mother-in-law had been stealing money?
“Your mother collected evidence. Before she could expose everything, she died in what everyone believed was an accident.”
“That’s what the police report said,” Brielle whispered.
“Your mother was terrified that the same people would come after you. She hid the original documents before she died.”
Margaret tried to stop me from leaving, but I pushed past her.
I found Carter waiting outside the boutique.
His expression changed when he saw the envelope in my hand.
“You’re buying baby clothes with another woman twelve days before our wedding, and your mother is threatening me inside a store. I think we’ve passed the point of having a private conversation.”
“Brielle is carrying my brother’s child.”
Carter had told me his younger brother, Nathan, died in a boating accident six years earlier.
Apparently, she had discovered she was pregnant shortly after Nathan’s death.
But the pregnancy wasn’t the only secret.
